summary: Master satellite-based disaster management. Learn SAR flood mapping, wildfire analysis, and AI-driven damage assessment. Enroll for expert-led training.
lede: Remote sensing and satellite technology in disaster management helps practitioners turn space-based Earth observation data into actionable intelligence for identifying, monitoring, and mitigating natural and man-made hazards. This intermediate-level course builds operational capability across data acquisition, pre-processing, feature extraction, change detection, and strategic reporting. You will practise selecting sensors for specific hazards, correcting optical data, analysing ground deformation with SAR interferometry, automating flood mapping, and developing multi-hazard susceptibility dashboards. Hands-on workflows using Google Earth Engine and SNAP address practical challenges such as cloud cover, data latency, and limited bandwidth, supporting rapid impact assessment and longer-term resilience planning.
audienceIntro: This program is tailored for professionals who already possess a foundational understanding of Geographic Information Systems and wish to specialize in the high-stakes domain of satellite-based disaster monitoring and response.
modules: Satellite Constellations and Disaster Management Foundations
Optical Data Processing for Environmental Hazards
Radar Remote Sensing for Flood and Water Hazards
Geological Hazards and Ground Deformation Analysis
AI and Automated Workflows in Disaster Response
Disaster Risk Reduction and Resilience Frameworks
prerequisites: Participants should have a working knowledge of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) principles and basic experience with geospatial software such as ArcGIS or QGIS. Familiarity with the fundamental concepts of electromagnetic radiation and basic statistical analysis is recommended. No prior programming experience is required, though an interest in cloud-based scripting will be beneficial for the advanced modules.
